cards.explanation: The answer is that He directs it where He pleases. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says the LORD directs the king's heart "…where He pleases." Picture a waterway: the water doesn't pick the route. Even the man wearing the crown has his heart in the LORD's hand.
The word is heart, friends. A man can walk his own road feeling great about it, and verse 2 says the LORD weighs the heart. He's not only looking at what we did. He's looking at what's underneath it.

The answer is False, friends. It goes the other way. The verse says, "To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice." Solomon puts the doing ahead of the offering. A gift with no righteous living behind it is like a cookie box with no cookies in it.
The answer is True, friends. Solomon says haughty eyes and a proud heart, the guides of the wicked, are sin. He doesn't call them a small slip. He just says sin, plain and simple.

Haste leads to poverty, friends. Solomon says the plans of the diligent bring plenty, "…as surely as haste leads to poverty." Careful plans on one side, rushing on the other. And he says it with total confidence.

The picture is a vanishing mist, friends. Solomon says a fortune made by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit. Like the steam off a fresh tray, you reach for it and your hand closes on nothing.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 7 says, "The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just." The thing they do ends up carrying them off. It's a heavy line, so it's worth reading slowly.

The conduct of the innocent is upright, friends. Verse 8 puts a crooked way next to the conduct of the innocent, which is upright. One road bends, and the other runs straight. Solomon sets them side by side so you can see the difference.

The answer is sharing a house with a quarrelsome wife, friends. Verse 9 says a corner of the roof is better than sharing a house with a quarrelsome wife. That's how strongly Solomon puts it. He'd take the cramped roof corner over the house.

Craves fits the first blank, friends. Verse 10 says the soul of the wicked man craves evil, which shows what he wants way down inside. Favor goes in the second blank. His neighbor "…finds no favor in his eyes." Solomon is showing how the wicked man sees the people around him.

The simple gain wisdom when a mocker is punished, friends. Verse 11 says when a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom. The punishment of the mocker is the moment Solomon names. The verse also says that when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.
The answer is True, friends. Verse 11 says, "…when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge." Even the wise keep learning. Nobody graduates from it.

He brings them to ruin, friends. Verse 12 says the Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin. Notice the verse says He considers their house. It's a serious line, so it's worth taking in quietly.

He too will cry out with no answer, friends. Verse 13 says whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, "…he too shall cry out and receive no answer." The very thing he did comes back around to him.
The word is secret, friends. Verse 14 says a gift in secret soothes anger. That's what Solomon observes about calming someone's anger. The verse adds that a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.

To the workers of iniquity, justice executed is a terror, friends. Verse 15 says justice executed is a joy to the righteous, "…but a terror to the workers of iniquity." The same justice lands very differently on each side.

The answer is False, friends. This one is heavy. Verse 16 says the man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead, not the living. The statement swaps in the wrong word.
The word is poor, friends. Verse 17 says he who loves pleasure will become poor. Loving pleasure ends up draining the pockets. The verse adds that the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.

The answer is False, friends, because it's reversed. Verse 18 says, "The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright." The wicked are the ransom there, not the righteous. That's a tough line.

A foolish man consumes them, friends. Verse 20 says precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, "…but a foolish man consumes them." The wise have it stored up, and the fool gets through it. Treasure on one side, consuming on the other.
The answer is False, friends. Verse 22 says a wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust. The thing they leaned on comes down.
The word is distress, friends. Verse 23 says he who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress. A watched tongue saves a lot of trouble. Solomon ties the mouth straight to the soul.
The slacker's craving kills him, friends. Verse 25 says the craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work. Notice the because: his hands refuse to work. It's a sober line.
The answer is True, friends. Verse 26 says all day long he covets more, "…but the righteous give without restraint." One keeps coveting more, and the other gives. Solomon puts them side by side.

It's even more detestable when it's brought with ill intent, friends. Verse 27 says the sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, "…how much more so when brought with ill intent!" The intent makes it worse.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 28 says a lying witness will perish, "…but the man who listens to truth will speak forever." The liar's words die with him, but the listener's words last. I think that's worth remembering: the one who listens well ends up with the word that outlives everybody else's.

The upright man makes his way sure, friends. Verse 29 says a wicked man hardens his face, "…but the upright man makes his way sure." One goes stiff and stubborn, and the other goes steady. I think the difference is that a hard face has stopped listening, while a sure way keeps moving forward.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 30 says, "There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD." Nothing on that list gets past Him. Wisdom, understanding and counsel all fall short against the LORD.

Victory is of the LORD, friends. Verse 31 says, "A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD." Getting the horse ready is a good thing to do, and the verse doesn't say to skip it. But the preparing and the victory are two different jobs, and the victory belongs to the LORD.
